data.narrative:
Vention, a Series C robotics and manufacturing platform founded by Etienne Lacroix and Max Windisch, has raised $95M+ to date. The valuation analysis draws on a comparison universe of 9 private peers (Hadrian, Agile Robots, Nimble Robotics, Divergent, Exotec, and others) and 1 public comparable, spanning the robotics and manufacturing sector.

Two valuation methods were applied. The stage-progression method, using total capital raised as a proxy baseline, applies a 1.7x step-up multiplier typical of Series C advancement, yielding $162M. The peer-median method anchors to three same-sector, same-stage comparables: Hadrian ($1.6B), Agile Robots ($1.0B), and Nimble Robotics ($1.0B), producing a median valuation of $1.0B with a range of $1.0B–$1.6B.

The triangulated analysis produces a range of $137M (low) to $1.1B (high), with a median of $581M. The wide spread reflects material divergence between stage-progression mechanics and peer-market valuations in this sector. Stage-progression offers a conservative floor anchored to capital efficiency; peer comparables suggest significantly higher valuations. Key uncertainties include revenue scale relative to peers, capital efficiency trajectories, and whether Vention's technology differentiation commands a premium within the robotics peer set.
